newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian financiers doubt inflation target.
newsitem.headline: Colombian financiers doubt inflation target.

text.p: Colombia is unlikely to reach its 1997 inflation target of 18 percent, although the economy could begin to pull out of its first recession in decades in the second half of this year, a influential financial group said in its latest weekly report.

The June consumer price index (CPI) is not due to be released until Wednesday, but the National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF) based its prediction on the peformance of the producer price index (PPI).
The June PPI figure, released last Friday was up 2.1 percent, taking the cumulative figure for the year to date to 12.2 percent and the figure for the last 12 months to 17.1 percent.

Colombia's CPI rose 1.62 percent in May compared with 1.55 percent in the same month last year, according to the National Statistics Department. The rise in the index is running at 9.94 percent for the period January through May compared to 12.75 percent in the same period last year.
The cumulative rise in the consumer price index for the last 12 months to the end of May was running at 18.6 percent.

"If the trend continues, the figure for the last 12 months to the end of June will be above 19 percent. And if that were not enough, the June PPI showed a substantial increase...," ANIF said in a report published by local media Monday.
"That probably means that not only has the chance of a further cut in interest rates disappeared, but so too has the chance of hitting the 1997 inflation target."

ANIF said 1997 inflation was likely to be higher than originally forecast by the central bank because of this year's wage rises, which were based on last year's inflation figure of 21.63 percent, and the "lack of credibility" in the 18 percent target set.
